To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the development of the Australian organic industry is being frustrated by the lack of a transformative capacity.
the development of the Australian organic industry was hindered by the absence of group and state capacity, which was further compounded by the absence of a deliberative network.
the absence of group and state capacity, and of deliberative venues, frustrates the development of the Australian organic industry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the capacity to transform the industry and to govern its development, and the ways in which the state can assist this process.
the role of transformative capacity in the development of an infant industry, in this case organic farming in Australia.
the question of what it takes to develop a new industry in a country like Australia, where the state is not particularly interventionist.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the absence of deliberative networking capacity has frustrated the capacity of the state to develop the organic farming industry.
the organic industry in Australia is in a very weak position in terms of transformative capacity, and is therefore unlikely to be able to develop into a strong and vibrant industry.
the Australian organic industry, as an infant industry, has not developed as well as it could have, and that this is in part due to the absence of transformative group capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transformative capacity is the ability to create and sustain the necessary institutional and social arrangements to enable the emergence of an industry.
the Australian organic industry has a long way to go before it is able to govern its own affairs.
the absence of deliberative networking capacity in industry development can be a significant constraint to transformative capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of industry is not only about the state’s capacity to intervene, but also the group’s capacity to engage in policy development.

transformative capacity is not only a matter of state capacity, but also of the capacity of industry organisations, and that deliberation is a key ingredient in the development of both state and industry organisation capacity.
industry development requires not only capable groups and a capable state, but also venues and spaces that foster deliberation and networking.
